items.text: Spread opens the same notes as the cockpit for a project-os repository: the same list, the same statuses, checked side by side on this repository. **2026-09-06:** Deck draws this repository's thirty notes as cards, read through the sidecar the cockpit itself was using, so the payload is the same one by construction. **2026-09-07:** the comparison is now a real one rather than a formality. Deck draws the sidecar's own groups as headings with counts, keeps what is owed at the top, folds finished work away and lists a note's children under it, so the two applications can be read against each other heading by heading ([[TASK-0023-The-Groups-The-Sidecar-Sends-Are-Drawn]], [[TST-0016-The-Groups-The-Sidecar-Sends-Are-Drawn]]). The side-by-side comparison a person makes is [[TST-0008-Spread-Opens-The-Same-Notes-As-The-Cockpit]], reworded the same day for the navigator. **Walked 2026-09-07:** Edwin marked it pass in the release ledger.

A popped-out panel carrying one thing, which is the Needs-you strip, a single note, or a desk, sits on a second display and is still there carrying the same thing after Deck is restarted. **2026-09-07, built:** pop out now asks what the window should carry and the answer is one of three panels, the panel travels in the address, and a restart reopens the window carrying the same panel on the display it was left on ([[TASK-0026-A-Popped-Out-Window-Carries-One-Panel]], [[TST-0020-A-Popped-Out-Window-Carries-One-Panel]]). The walk needs a second monitor and is [[TST-0009-A-Status-Window-Survives-A-Restart-On-A-Second-Display]], reworded the same day to name the status window again. **Restored 2026-09-07:** on 2026-09-06 this criterion was amended down to "a popped-out window", because Deck has no status panel and a pop-out is the same view again with no navigation. Edwin's decision on 2026-09-07 is that the application should be changed to match the criterion rather than the other way round, so the status window is back and [[TASK-0026-A-Popped-Out-Window-Carries-One-Panel]] builds it. **2026-09-06:** the placement half is built, and the decision is a pure function tested over display sets including an unplugged monitor ([[TST-0003-A-Window-Is-Placed-On-The-Display-It-Was-On]]). The walk needs a second monitor and is [[TST-0009-A-Status-Window-Survives-A-Restart-On-A-Second-Display]], whose Procedure goes back to naming a status window when TASK-0026 lands. **Walked 2026-09-07:** Edwin marked [[TST-0009-A-Status-Window-Survives-A-Restart-On-A-Second-Display]] pass in the release ledger.

Deck served over the local network opens in Safari on a tablet, reads the notes, and refuses every write at its own host. **2026-09-06:** the host is built and the refusal is tested over real HTTP, including methods a browser will not send; `--lan` binds it beyond loopback. The tablet itself is [[TST-0010-Deck-Opens-Read-Only-On-A-Tablet]]. **Walked 2026-09-07:** Edwin marked it pass in the release ledger. **Reopened 2026-09-08:** that pass is invalidated in the ledger and the criterion is unticked, because the fixes of 2026-09-07 changed two things inside this claim — what a tablet gets while a sidecar is still indexing, and what Deck's host will forward. The check now walks both.

Every view in Deck's switcher comes from the view provider for the workspace kind, the renderer holds no fixed list of view names, and for a project-os repository the list matches the cockpit's navigator. **Evidence, 2026-09-06:** [[TST-0006-Views-Come-From-The-Provider-And-Match-The-Cockpit]] pins the list against a fixture read off the cockpit's own navigator and searches the built renderer for every view name; the running application drew Overview, Intent, Features, Issues, Tests, Publication and Library.

An address copied out of Deck and pasted back into it restores the same view, the same desk and the same focused note. **Evidence, 2026-09-06:** [[TST-0005-Every-State-Round-Trips-Through-Its-Address]] round-trips a table of states and refuses twelve malformed ones; in the running application the copy control produced an address that parsed, named the open workspace and carried the focused note.

Every row of the cockpit's capability register that Spread relies on is marked `adopted` in `docs/reference/cockpit-adoption.md`, with the register re-read on the day the phase closes. **Re-read 2026-09-07, the closing day:** the cockpit is still at commit `c0ed9e3` and has landed no change note since the previous read, so no key arrived and no row moved. The keys were compared mechanically rather than by eye: the register lists 55, [[REFERENCE-COCKPIT-ADOPTION]] carries 55, and neither side holds a key the other lacks. The nine rows Spread relies on — `surface.shell`, `shell.workspaces.rail`, `shell.workspaces.discovery`, `shell.nav.modes`, `shell.reader.render`, `shell.windows`, `api.read.nav`, `api.read.note` and `api.read.record` — are all `adopted`, as are `shell.nav.needs-you`, `shell.nav.hide-completed`, `shell.stage.find` and `api.guards`. The dated line is in that note's Maintenance section. **2026-09-06:** the register was read and twelve rows moved.

**Added 2026-09-08. Met 2026-09-09.** The seven project-os views are seven descriptions and draw exactly what they draw today, checked against the fixture read off the cockpit's own navigator ([[TST-0006-Views-Come-From-The-Provider-And-Match-The-Cockpit]], [[TST-0030-A-Description-Parses-Or-Says-Why-Not]]). A difference that looks like an improvement is still a difference and still fails this criterion. **Evidence:** the fixture check is unedited and passes — the same seven ids and labels, in the cockpit's order. All seven parse with zero refusals, each naming `list` and `spread` and none naming `glass`. The smoke run drew the same two headings and the same thirteen rows before and after the change. The one thing the shape could not carry is Overview, which is a page of statistics rather than a view of notes; it is written in Deck's own extension namespace and the finding is in [[TASK-0042-Seven-Descriptions-Equal-To-Todays-Views]] rather than hidden in a workaround.

**Added 2026-09-08. Built 2026-09-09; the walk is owed.** A `.base` file from `~/Notes` reads as a Deck description, and every construct the evaluator does not support is named on screen — never an empty list with no explanation. Walked in [[TST-0027-A-Base-File-Reads-As-A-Description-And-The-Seven-Views-Are-Unchanged]] against three files of different shapes, including the TaskNotes plugin's own view types. **What is proved already:** all thirteen live base files — eleven from `~/Notes`, two from the cockpit's `docs/__bases__/` — read as descriptions, and every unsupported construct comes back named with its location. The TaskNotes plugin's four view types are reported without stopping the file. The unsupported report is drawn above the list rather than instead of it. **What is NOT proved:** that a vault's base file becomes a view a person can click, because the Vault PROVIDER is [[PHASE-0003-Vault]] and only the parser was built here. The walk is what says whether the parser half is enough to judge.

**Added 2026-09-08. Built 2026-09-09; the walk is owed.** A criterion ticked in Deck, with evidence, is ticked in the file and shows as ticked in the cockpit, and one status transition made in Deck moves the note's status the same way. Walked in [[TST-0028-A-Criterion-Ticked-In-Deck-Is-Ticked-In-The-Cockpit]] with `git diff` beside it, so the claim is about the file and not about two screens. **What is proved already:** both writes were made against the real sidecar this repository runs, on 2026-09-09, and reverted with `git checkout`. `ISS-0016` moved `triage` → `deferred` in the file with the sidecar's decision callout appended; a criterion was written as `- [x] … — evidence: … (actor, date)`, the sidecar's own `TICK_TEMPLATE`. **What is NOT proved and is why this stays unticked:** nobody has done it through Deck's own reader, with the cockpit open beside it, which is the half of the claim about two applications agreeing.

**Added 2026-09-08. Built 2026-09-09; the tablet walk is owed.** The served page offers no verb at all: not greyed out, absent. Checked on a real tablet in [[TST-0028-A-Criterion-Ticked-In-Deck-Is-Ticked-In-The-Cockpit]] and asserted in the smoke run, and Deck's host still answers 405 to every method that is not a read ([[ADR-0003-Deck-Writes-Through-The-Shell]]). **What is proved already:** the served host answers `write: false` and the shell answers `write: true`, both in the smoke run; the renderer's verbs sit behind that capability and the bridge they would use does not exist on a served page at all; and every method that is not `GET` or `HEAD` is refused 405 over real HTTP on seven paths, including the new records path and the two write paths. **What is NOT proved:** that a person looking at the page on a tablet sees nothing where a verb would be. That is a walk.

**Added 2026-09-08. Met 2026-09-09.** An address carrying the new keys — `surface`, `page`, `flow` and `step` — round-trips, and each key refuses a value it does not know. Every address that parsed before still parses to the same state, and an address naming an unregistered panel kind is refused until that kind is registered ([[TST-0034-The-Grammar-Carries-The-New-Keys-And-The-Panel-Registry-Refuses-Strangers]]). **Evidence:** 15 checks. The six round-trip states and the twelve malformed addresses moved into one file both suites read, so "nothing regressed" is a measurement over one table rather than over a copy of it, and the written form of an address with none of the new keys is byte-for-byte what it was. The load-bearing check refuses `?panel=acceptance-checks`, registers that kind, and parses the same address again.

The current collection and full authored document share the Glass desk with exact membership, stable identity, chosen reading size, protected input and a reliable return to the selected row. TST-0063 is walked with real-scale data, keyboard, reduced motion and the read-only narrow/tablet route. Historical fixed-navigator evidence below does not discharge this new criterion. Automated evidence, 2026-10-02: [[TST-0068-The-Glass-Desktop-Is-Walked-With-A-Real-Pointer]], [[TST-0069-The-Collection-Holds-Still-When-Notes-Change-On-Disk]] and [[TST-0072-Glass-Is-Measured-At-The-Size-Of-A-Real-Workspace]] are scripted walks with a real pointer and keyboard in a Linux box, the last on a copy of `your-trainer`, 3,269 notes. They cover membership, identity, the chosen size, the keyboard, reduced motion and the served page in a narrow window. Not ticked: [[TST-0063-A-Collection-And-Full-Note-Share-Glass]] is a person's walk and has not been walked, and no tablet was used.

The continuity repair in TASK-0104 satisfies ISS-0070/71/72 and the revised TST-0052: no duplicated spatial note or ghost, no size jump on movement, and the neighbourhood moves with its document. Automated evidence, 2026-10-02: the three issues are `fixed` on the smoke run's Glass section ([[TST-0045-Glass-Is-Driven-With-A-Real-Pointer]]) and the neighbourhood walk, whose checks are in [[TASK-0104-Preserve-Note-Identity-Size-And-Neighbourhood-While-Moving]]. Not ticked: [[TST-0052-A-Note-Opens-In-The-Middle-Of-Its-Neighbours-And-The-Wheel-Zooms]] is a person's walk and has not been walked. One choice in [[ISS-0072-Moving-The-Note-In-The-Middle-Throws-The-Arrangement-Away]] is Edwin's: a dragged document stops at the field's edge with its header in sight, where his answer of 2026-09-12 was that nothing is clamped.

Stack/table/cards and Read/Compare/Show related preserve exact members, document sizes and live content. Preview, cancel, apply and layout-only undo satisfy TST-0064 with foreground rendering measurements. Automated evidence, 2026-10-02: [[TST-0071-Collection-Forms-And-Arrangements-Are-Walked-With-A-Real-Pointer]] is a scripted walk of the three forms and the three arrangements, and [[TST-0072-Glass-Is-Measured-At-The-Size-Of-A-Real-Workspace]] times a turn after each arrangement. Not ticked: [[TST-0064-Glass-Collections-And-Arrangements-Stay-Exact]] has not been walked, and every time was taken in a box that draws in software, so there is no foreground measurement on the Mac.

FEAT-0023's scene and handoff contracts are decided and its eventual acceptance walk records restoration, fresh query membership and recovery from an unavailable display. Its feature-only backlog note is expanded before implementation; it is not a prerequisite for delivering FEAT-0020. Planned 2026-10-02: the contracts are proposed in ADR-0007 and not yet accepted by Edwin, the note is expanded, and the walk is [[TST-0073-A-Scene-Reopens-And-A-Note-Crosses-Screens]], unwalked. Built the same day. Automated evidence: [[TST-0076-Scenes-And-Handoff-Are-Walked-With-A-Real-Pointer]] is a scripted walk of saving, reopening with fresh membership, both undos, and a handoff to a desk window and a reader window, on this repository and on `your-trainer`. A display that went away was simulated by sending the event Electron sends; no display was unplugged and the box has one screen. Not ticked: the contracts are not accepted and the walk is not walked.

Deck opens a workspace in Glass: the owed notes are in front, the view's subject fills the middle and the outer field, and the quiet band is behind you. **Every note the view holds is in a band or counted on screen, and no band is silently short.** The walk is [[TST-0023-Glass-Opens-First-And-A-Days-Notes-Are-Read-In-It]]. Automated evidence, 2026-09-10: [[TST-0045-Glass-Is-Driven-With-A-Real-Pointer]] opens an address with no surface in Glass, with owed notes in front, the view either side and the quiet band on the canvas behind with its count on the compass. The walk is Edwin's.

Switching view re-arranges the same cards, and no note is dropped into the quiet band because a nearer band was full: overflow is stated on screen. Evidence, 2026-09-10: [[TST-0045-Glass-Is-Driven-With-A-Real-Pointer]] (11 of 12 cards kept their elements across a switch and moved, none reused, no per-card delay) and [[TST-0040-The-Field-Deals-Every-View-Into-Three-Bands]] (every owed note in front or counted, Your Trainer's overflow counted); the bar says "and N more in front — all listed in the navigator".

Lifting a note brings its neighbourhood into the front band, the front plane says what it now means, and with two or more notes on the desk the field marks what they share. The walk is [[TST-0024-A-Note-Is-Lifted-And-Its-Neighbourhood-Arrives]]. Automated evidence, 2026-09-10: [[TST-0045-Glass-Is-Driven-With-A-Real-Pointer]] (11 of 11 neighbours in front, the label, the owed count unmoved, the shared set marked and counted). The walk is Edwin's. **Amended 2026-09-11 ([[FEAT-0017-An-Opened-Note-Stands-In-The-Middle-Of-Its-Neighbours]]):** a lift first puts the note in the middle with its neighbourhood on a ring around it; the neighbourhood takes the front band once the note leaves the middle.

A note lifted in Glass is on the same desk in Spread, and a card dragged in Spread is on the desk in Glass. Evidence, 2026-09-10: [[TST-0045-Glass-Is-Driven-With-A-Real-Pointer]] — panes lifted in Glass are Spread's cards at the same positions, and a card dragged in Spread is a pane at its new place in Glass.

Every card visible in a Glass arrangement can be reached and opened from the navigator using only the keyboard. Evidence, 2026-09-10: [[TST-0045-Glass-Is-Driven-With-A-Real-Pointer]] — Tab, arrows and Enter lift a note; held notes, neighbours and shared notes have navigator groups; in the orbit the navigator lists all 24 cards and every note with no link.

A Glass address pasted back into Deck restores the same view, the same surface and the same focused note. Evidence, 2026-09-10: [[TST-0045-Glass-Is-Driven-With-A-Real-Pointer]] — an address copied in Glass (no surface key, the note named) opened again restores Glass, the view and the note; `surface=spread` restores the desk; [[TST-0043-The-Hands-State-Is-Shared-And-Never-Kept]] for the grammar.

Glass opens in Safari on the tablet served by Deck's host, with no `backdrop-filter` over the moving field. **Amended 2026-09-10:** and the tablet shows the desk the Mac holds, following the store over Deck's host by reading alone, with every write still refused 405. Automated evidence, 2026-09-10: [[TST-0039-The-Served-Page-Follows-The-Store-By-Reading]] and the smoke run — a page with no bridge received a lifted note within a second, the two routes refuse five methods with 405 from the network address, and [[TST-0042-Nothing-Blurs-And-Only-Near-Cards-Are-Promoted]] holds the stylesheet to no `backdrop-filter`. Safari on the tablet is a person's step.

**Added 2026-09-10.** A person arranges the field by hand and it behaves as stated: a pulled note stands in the front band across a view switch, a pushed note is behind them, an owed note cannot be pushed out and the refusal says why, the front plane counts what a hand placed, panes keep their place and size across a restart while the pulled and pushed sets do not, and `git status` in the workspace is unchanged afterwards. The walk is [[TST-0038-The-Field-Is-Arranged-By-Hand-And-A-Note-Is-Thrown-To-Another-Screen]]. Automated evidence, 2026-09-10: [[TST-0045-Glass-Is-Driven-With-A-Real-Pointer]] (pull across a view switch, push, refused push with its sentence, the counts, panes across a reload, `git status` unchanged) and [[TST-0043-The-Hands-State-Is-Shared-And-Never-Kept]] (the sets are dropped on restart). The walk is Edwin's.

**Added 2026-09-10.** A note flicked off the field toward a second display opens in the reader window there, or opens a new one on an empty display, with the flight going toward that screen and the target named while the drag approached the edge; the same throw reaches the tablet. Same walk. Automated evidence, 2026-09-10: [[TST-0045-Glass-Is-Driven-With-A-Real-Pointer]] throws into a reader window, onto a desk panel and onto a display with no Deck window, which opened a reader there; the strip named the targets. The walk, on a second display and the tablet, is Edwin's.

**Added 2026-09-10.** After a week of daily use in Glass, Edwin records from the compass how often he turned to look behind and whether anything was lost there. The DES-0002 review said this question should be a criterion rather than a remark, because the literature expects a "behind you" band to become a place things are forgotten, and pushing by hand makes that easier. Either answer is a result, and a bad one is what would retire the quiet band's placement, not the phase. Edwin's, after a week of use; nothing automated stands in for it.

The frame time while turning is measured on the fleet's largest workspace in a foreground window and written as a number in [[FEAT-0009-The-Field-Where-Depth-Carries-Priority]], with the pooled-versus-canvas choice recorded beside it. If the number fails on a laptop, Spread returns to being the default and this note says so. Evidence, 2026-09-10: written in [[FEAT-0009-The-Field-Where-Depth-Carries-Priority]], "Measured": Your Trainer held the display's 16.7 ms median frame (17.0 ms at the 95th percentile) with two panes held and a reach drawn, 2.2 ms of script work per frame, 286 tiles and 2,303 elements at most, window in front; the hybrid is kept. Taken on a Mac Studio, not a laptop: the laptop reading is owed, and the throttled run (6.6 ms of work at 4× CPU cost) is an estimate.

[[FEAT-0001-The-Corpus-Has-An-Inside]]'s two other measurements are written as numbers: the size and time of the one request that returns the whole edge list, and the position drift when a note is added and the layout recomputed. A planted orphan and a single-edge cluster are visible in the orbit arrangement ([[TST-0025-A-Planted-Orphan-And-A-Single-Edge-Cluster-Are-Visible]]). A measurement that fails costs the orbit arrangement, not the field, and is recorded here as an outcome. The numbers are written, 2026-09-10, in [[FEAT-0001-The-Corpus-Has-An-Inside]], "Measured": the one request is 2.39 MB and 86 ms cold on the cockpit's 1,549 notes, and the drift when a note is added is 0 on every corpus. The orphan band and the bridge colour are built and [[TST-0047-The-Orbit-Layout-Is-Solved-Once-And-Kept]] finds a planted orphan and a planted cluster; the walk [[TST-0025-A-Planted-Orphan-And-A-Single-Edge-Cluster-Are-Visible]] is Edwin's.

Edwin has chosen the orbit arrangement's treatment, and [[TASK-0005-The-Treatment-Is-Chosen-Not-Assumed]] records the choice and its cost. All three are drawn and switchable on 2026-09-10; the choice is Edwin's.

Edwin does one real task in Deck instead of the cockpit, for example triaging a day's issues across two screens, and records which of the two he would rather have used and why. The walk is [[TST-0015-One-Real-Task-Done-In-Deck-Instead-Of-The-Cockpit]], moved here from [[PHASE-0001-Deck]] on 2026-09-07 because his first attempt came back as a question: it cannot be answered until the functionality is there. Either answer is a valid result.

The console decision is recorded as an ADR naming what was evaluated (T3 Code's terminal against the cockpit's), what was measured, and what was chosen. ([[ADR-0009-Deck-Runs-Its-Own-Agent-Sessions-Drawn-As-Conversations]], 2026-10-22)
Several consoles are open at once in Deck, each a slab that drags, resizes and fades on its own, and a console survives a Deck restart the way the cockpit's tmux session does.

Every row of the cockpit's capability register is `adopted`, `replaced by` or `not applicable` in [[REFERENCE-COCKPIT-ADOPTION]], with a reason on every `not applicable`, and the register re-read on the day the phase closes.
Every verb Deck offers goes through the sidecar's existing guards, and the served host still refuses every method that is not a read.
`~/Notes` opens in Deck as a workspace, discovered by its `.obsidian` directory.
The Comics notes arrive typed: characters, pages, panels, locations and chapters appear under their own types, and the count matches the 43 typed Comics notes measured on 2026-09-06.
The four Comic base views — Characters, Chapters, Locations, Pages — appear as Deck views, each with the base's own filter, sort and card image.
A base using anything outside the supported subset renders as "not supported" and names the expression it could not read.
The supported Bases subset is named in a note in this repository.
The four Comics `.canvas` files open as Spread boards, and a session of browsing the vault leaves `git status` in `~/Notes` unchanged.
What needs attention in a world is decided and written down, and the vault's front plane shows it.
DES-0005 is accepted by Edwin, with one plate per screen S1 to S7, drawn from Deck's and your-trainer's real tickets.

Deck opens on the wheel for both workspaces. Every ticket the overview model returns is drawn exactly once, and the counts on screen equal the model's counts (automated). Evidence: TST-0090 on both fixtures; TST-0093's window run on 2026-10-14 drew 377 of 377 tickets on Deck and 2,747 of 2,747 on your-trainer.

Every screen S1 to S7 passes the look's checks 1, 2 and 5: at most 60 words at rest, no number without a mark, an address that restores it and a list twin (automated, on both workspaces). Evidence: `checkScene` in TST-0090 (S1 to S4) and the overview-flows suite (S5 to S7) on both workspaces, and TST-0094 on every plate; words at rest range from 5 to 37.

From the wheel, a phase, a ticket, a design, a release test check and a feature gate are each reached in at most two clicks, and by keyboard alone. Evidence: a sector opens its phase and a wedge its ticket (one click; TST-0093); on a ticket's screen its glyph opens its design, release test or gate (two clicks), and an owed-again badge opens the release test in one. Tab reaches every sector, disc and control, and the arrow keys and Enter reach and open all 361 and 2,747 tickets (Codex's round-two review of FEAT-0027).
Edwin accepts a design in S5, records a Pass and a Fail in S6 and accepts a feature in S7, and each verdict appears in the cockpit. The same verbs from an agent session are refused.

Each feature has an independent review by the agent that did not build it, recorded on the feature. Evidence: two rounds each, Claude reviewing FEAT-0026 and FEAT-0029, Codex (GPT-6 Astra) reviewing FEAT-0025, FEAT-0027 and FEAT-0028; verdicts and fixes are under each feature's Review.
Edwin's acceptance tests for each feature pass, including whether the screens read as pictures rather than text.
